one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-11-18 to 2026-12-17 holds no Netflix earnings (Q4 results come around 2027-01-20) and no guidance event. Scheduled: the Thanksgiving Eve NFL game on 2026-11-25, the first live test of ad sales after the ~$300M cut to the 2026 ad goal [22]; the December FOMC; Christmas NFL games fall after the window. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways: intermediate-term losers keep underperforming (Jegadeesh-Titman [25]) and stocks far from their 52-week high lag (George-Hwang [24]; NFLX is 48% below its $115.25 high and at a 52-week low), drift after the Q3 guide miss is negative (Bernard-Thomas [26]; Zacks Q4 EPS revisions 0 up / 10 down in four weeks [11]), while one-month reversal after an -11% month offsets part of it. So: a nearly symmetric lognormal, median $59.40 (-0.5%), monthly sigma 10.5% (36% annual / 3.5, rounded up for the post-earnings re-rating).

fair_value.method: P/E 16.82x (peer median 18.92x shrunk toward NFLX's own 16.33x, k = 0.8) on the driver model's own NTM GAAP EPS at 2027-11-17 (~$4.27: FY2028 revenue $60.6B, EBIT margin 34.5%, ~3.96B shares) = $71.90.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM GAAP EPS at the horizon ~$4.27 (FY2027 EPS ~$3.85, FY2028 ~$4.40 vs Zacks consensus 3.74 / 4.43 [11], on revenue $55.9B / $60.6B and EBIT margin 33.5% / 34.5%, tax 16%, shares -4.3%/yr) x 16.82x

inputs_detail.derivation: TTM effective rate 2,933.7 / 17,700.3 = 16.6% (F81/F88), which includes tax on the $2.85B WBD termination fee; Q3'26 653.0/4,316.9 = 15.1% (F82/F89); FY2025 1,741.4/12,722.6 = 13.7%. 16% sits inside that range and within 1pt of the TTM anchor (global minimum tax keeps it from returning to 2025's 13.7%).
Debt 15,132.4 (F96) - cash 8,194.3 (F90) - ST investments 28.7 (F91). Leases not included (operating leases are in operating cash flow).
Cover-page shares 4,106.3M (F95) + option/RSU dilution 60.6M (Q3'26 diluted wavg 4,195.1M F33 - basic wavg 4,134.5M from XBRL [10]).

Buybacks: Q3'26 63.9M shares for $4.8B [1]; TTM $12.9B (F67); $22.3B authorization left [1]. Path: FCF from Q4'26 to the horizon (~$2.5B Q4'26 + ~$11.8B of 2027 to mid-Nov) plus ~$0.6B of cash draw = ~$14.9B at a stated ~$66 average price (between today's $59.68 and the base value) = ~226M retired; issuance ~25M (SBC $540M TTM F46 at ~$60 plus option exercises). Net -201M over 1.13 years from 4,167M = -4.3%/yr.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At today's $59.68 the same dollars retire ~250M shares (-4.8%/yr), about +$0.4/share; if buybacks slow to FCF minus a cash rebuild, -3%/yr, about -$1/share.

anchor.note: Q3'26 diluted wavg 4,195.1 vs Q3'25 4,340.4 = -3.3% y/y; the path is faster because 2026 buybacks ran at a record rate and the price is lower

inputs_detail.derivation: Peer median NTM P/E 18.92x (refresh table: DIS 16.64, SONY 17.66, META 18.56, GOOGL 19.29, AMZN 24.73, SPOT 38.86 [14]); own NTM 16.33x (59.68/3.655 [14]); exit = 18.92 x (16.33/18.92)^0.8 = 16.82x (k = 0.8 default). Base-rate cross-check: NFLX's 2022 trough was ~15.6x trailing (Jun-2022 close $17.49 [15] / FY2021 EPS $1.124 split-adjusted [10]), so 16.8x is near the bottom of its own history, as fits revenue growth slowing to high single digits.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Legacy-media de-rating (DIS ~16.6x [14], PYPL-style compression to ~12x as growth slowed in 2022-23 [16]) is the downside case; a re-rating back to 20x+ needs re-accelerating engagement.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Cross-check only: peer median 18.92x x consensus NTM EPS at the horizon ~$4.37 (0.12 x FY2027 3.74 + 0.88 x FY2028 4.43, Nasdaq/Zacks [11]) = $82.7

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Base-rate cross-check only: median 12-month return after a -40%+ year in six analog episodes (NFLX 2004-10, 2011-11, 2022-05; META 2022-10; PYPL 2022-05; DIS 2022-12) is +63% (range -27% to +223%) [15][16]; $59.68 x 1.63 = $97. Not weighted: the sample is small and picked from famous rebounds; the two maturity de-ratings (PYPL -27%, DIS +4%) fit today's setup (earnings still growing ~20%, revenue growth slowing) better.

downside.story: 10th percentile: engagement keeps losing to YouTube (US TV share 8.8% to 7.7% in a year [18][19]), the 2027 ad launch slips like 2026's [1], members flat in UCAN: revenue growth ~6.5% in 2027 and ~5.5% in 2028; content trimmed 2% but margin still ~2pts lower; the market prices Netflix as mature media at ~11.8x (DIS 16.6x [14]; PYPL fell from ~20x to ~12x as growth slowed and kept falling 27% in the 12 months after a -67% year [16]). A 2027 recession (Kalshi 20% [17]) adds ad and churn pressure.

base.story: Median: Q4'26 at the guide (-0.3%), FY2027 revenue +9.4% to $55.9B (consensus $56.6B [13]) as price, members and ads each add a few points while engagement stays flat; EBIT margin 33.5% in 2027 and 34.5% in 2028 (consensus 33.3% / 35.1%); FCF returned through buybacks (-4.3% shares a year); P/E holds near today's 16-17x.

upside.story: 90th percentile: a 2027 US price round plus ads in 15 more countries take growth back to ~11.5% (above consensus +10.7% [13]) and margins to ~36% by 2028; the market re-rates toward its 2024-25 range (21.8x, still below the 2023-25 history), as after NFLX's own -40%+ years in 2004, 2011 and 2022 when the stock gained 27-179% in the next 12 months [15].

sbc_treatment.note: FY2025 SBC $368.4M (F43; TTM $540.1M F46); GAAP EBIT and EPS carry it, peers' P/E is on GAAP-like EPS (one-offs out), share count falls only by net buybacks after issuance.

reasoning: Lane: base rates, history, events. (1) What happened: revenue growth slowed four quarters running (16.2% to 11.8%, Q4 guide 11.5%), the 2026 ad goal was cut to ~$2.7B, H1 view hours grew 2% and Netflix's US TV share fell from 8.8% to 7.7% while YouTube hit 15.8% [1][6][18][19]; the stock fell 46% in a year to a 52-week low. Earnings still grow ~20% and FCF (~$12B) all goes to buybacks. (2) Guidance record: first annual revenue guides were beaten by +1.5% (FY2024) and +3.9% (FY2025), margins by 2.7 and 1.5pts, but FY2026 lands inside its first range and on its 31.5% margin guide, and quarterly beats have shrunk to ~0.1-0.8%: the beat habit has ended, so we do not add one [4][7][8][9]. (3) Build: regional y/y growth (members, price, ads) fading by ~1pt a year per the growth-persistence evidence [23] to +9.4% in 2027 and +8.4% in 2028 (1-2.5% under consensus [13]); cost of revenues +7.5%/+7%, opex +6% on a base cleared of deal and layoff costs, giving 33.5% / 34.5% margins (consensus 33.3% / 35.1%). (4) Value: P/E 16.82x on our NTM EPS ~$4.27 (3.97B shares at the horizon; consensus NTM ~$4.35) = $71.90. NFLX's own 2022 trough was ~15.6x trailing [10][15], so the exit multiple already sits at the low end of its history. (5) Distribution: after -40%+ years the six analogs returned a median +63% but the two maturity de-ratings (PYPL -27%, DIS +4%) are the closer fit [15][16]; Kalshi prices a 2027 recession at 20% [17]. Downside (P10) $43.24 cuts growth 3pts and the multiple to ~11.8x; upside (P90) $104.37 adds 2pts of growth and re-rates to ~21.8x. The left tail is fatter. Not driver-linked: none (one P/E leg). Research limits: Zacks, MarketBeat, chartmill and Northeast Times pages were blocked; consensus revenue came from MarketScreener, EPS from Nasdaq/Zacks.

drivers.derivation: Actuals: 2025-26 quarters from the regional tables (Q4'24 letter [7] for 2024 bases, Q4'25 letter [4], Q3'26 letter [1]); Q3'26 +11% reported/FX-neutral. Q4'26 +10.5%: inside the Q4 total guide of +11.5% [1] but a touch below it because the 2026 ad goal was cut to ~$2.7B from ~$3B on slower ad-product rollout [1][22] and H1 view hours grew only 2% [6]. FY2027 +8.5% = paid members ~+2.5% (US TV share fell from 8.8% in Jul-2025 to 7.7% in Aug-2026 per Nielsen [18][19], so little household growth) + price/mix ~+4% (2026 price changes 'consistent with prior adjustments' [1]) + ads ~+2pts (US ad market +12.3% in 2026 per IAB [20]; Netflix ads a small share of revenue). FY2028 +7.5%: one point lower, base-rate fade (large-cap revenue growth regresses to the mean, Chan-Karceski-Lakonishok [23]).
drivers.variant_view: Upside: a new US price round in 2027 plus ads doubling would hold UCAN at ~+11% (consensus FY2027 total +10.7% [13]), about +$4/share; downside: engagement keeps sliding vs YouTube and growth falls to ~5%, about -$6/share.
drivers.why: UCAN is ~44% of revenue and the market where price increases and ads matter most; the disclosed regional line is informative because Netflix stopped reporting members and ARM in 2025, so regional revenue is the finest volume x price evidence left.

Q4'26 7,040 (+7.9% y/y): Q4 guide operating income $3.5B on $13.44B revenue [1] with opex ~$2.9B leaves ~$7.0B; content amortization guided to grow ~10% in 2026 [4] and 9M cost of revenues grew 7.5% (18,004 vs 16,753 [10]). drivers.variant_view: Variant: content amortization grows at the 2026 guide of ~10% [4] in 2027: about -1.2pts of margin, roughly -$3/share; or cost discipline after the 6% layoff [21] holds growth to 5%, about +$3/share.
drivers.why: Content spend is the largest cost and sets gross margin; it is management's main lever.

FY2027 +7.5% and FY2028 +7%: content cash spend at ~1.1x amortization [1][4] keeps amortization rising high single digits, plus live sports (NFL Christmas and Thanksgiving games [22]); not a past step: 2026 quarters ran +11.9%, +13.4%, -1.4%, +7.9%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Variant: content amortization grows at the 2026 guide of ~10% [4] in 2027: about -1.2pts of margin, roughly -$3/share; or cost discipline after the 6% layoff [21] holds growth to 5%, about +$3/share.

inputs_detail.derivation: Actuals from XBRL marketing + technology & development + G&A [10] (Q1-Q3'26 2,405 / 2,331 / 2,336). Q4'26 2,900 incl. ~$160M of headcount-reduction cost (120bps of Q4 margin [1]). FY2027 = 2026 underlying (Q1 ex ~$150M WBD deal cost [4][5]: 2,255 / 2,331 / 2,336 / 2,740) x 1.06: the ~1,000-person (6%) layoff [21] offsets wage and ad-tech build-out. FY2028 x 1.065.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Variant: opex grows with the 2026 rate (+11% in Q3'26 [10]), about -$2/share.

inputs_detail.derivation: TTM effective rate 2,933.7 / 17,700.3 = 16.6% (F81/F88), which includes tax on the $2.85B WBD termination fee; Q3'26 653.0/4,316.9 = 15.1% (F82/F89); FY2025 1,741.4/12,722.6 = 13.7%. 16% sits inside that range and within 1pt of the TTM anchor (global minimum tax keeps it from returning to 2025's 13.7%).
TTM interest expense 856.9 / gross debt 15,132.4 = 5.66%; applied to net debt as the engine's carry cost (conservative: cash earns interest that is ignored).
Debt 15,132.4 (F96) - cash 8,194.3 (F90) - ST investments 28.7 (F91). Leases not included (operating leases are in operating cash flow).
Cover-page shares 4,106.3M (F95) + option/RSU dilution 60.6M (Q3'26 diluted wavg 4,195.1M F33 - basic wavg 4,134.5M from XBRL [10]).

Buybacks: Q3'26 63.9M shares for $4.8B [1]; TTM $12.9B (F67); $22.3B authorization left [1]. Path: FCF from Q4'26 to the horizon (~$2.5B Q4'26 + ~$11.8B of 2027 to mid-Nov) plus ~$0.6B of cash draw = ~$14.9B at a stated ~$66 average price (between today's $59.68 and the base value) = ~226M retired; issuance ~25M (SBC $540M TTM F46 at ~$60 plus option exercises). Net -201M over 1.13 years from 4,167M = -4.3%/yr.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At today's $59.68 the same dollars retire ~250M shares (-4.8%/yr), about +$0.4/share; if buybacks slow to FCF minus a cash rebuild, -3%/yr, about -$1/share.

anchor.note: Q3'26 diluted wavg 4,195.1 vs Q3'25 4,340.4 = -3.3% y/y; the path is faster because 2026 buybacks ran at a record rate and the price is lower

inputs_detail.derivation: TTM D&A 392.2 / revenue 49,734.6 = 0.79% (content amortization sits in cost of revenues, not here).

TTM capex 932.9/49,734.6 = 1.88%; FY2025 688.2/45,183 = 1.52%; 1.7% between them. The Q4'26 real-estate purchase that cut the FCF guide by ~$0.5B [1] is carried as a one-off adjustment, not in the ratio.

Content cash spend runs ~1.1x amortization [1][4], so operating cash flow trails earnings as revenue grows. FY2025: CFO 10,149.3 vs NI 10,981.2 + D&A 333.4 + SBC 368.4 = 11,683.0, a 1,533.7 gap on 6,182 of revenue growth = 0.25; 9M 2026 gap 2.86B (includes tax timing on the WBD fee). 0.30 sits between.
TTM SBC 540.1/49,734.6 = 1.09%; GAAP EBIT already carries it (cost basis).
Netflix returns essentially all FCF through buybacks (TTM buybacks $12.9B F67 vs TTM FCF $11.4B F99; $22.3B authorization [1]). Set at the model's own FCFF margin so net debt stays near $7B.

Peer median NTM P/E 18.92x (refresh table: DIS 16.64, SONY 17.66, META 18.56, GOOGL 19.29, AMZN 24.73, SPOT 38.86 [14]); own NTM 16.33x (59.68/3.655 [14]); exit = 18.92 x (16.33/18.92)^0.8 = 16.82x (k = 0.8 default). Base-rate cross-check: NFLX's 2022 trough was ~15.6x trailing (Jun-2022 close $17.49 [15] / FY2021 EPS $1.124 split-adjusted [10]), so 16.8x is near the bottom of its own history, as fits revenue growth slowing to high single digits.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Legacy-media de-rating (DIS ~16.6x [14], PYPL-style compression to ~12x as growth slowed in 2022-23 [16]) is the downside case; a re-rating back to 20x+ needs re-accelerating engagement.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2026 FCF guide cut to ~$12.0B from ~$12.5B 'due primarily to the expected closing of a real estate transaction in Q4' [1]: ~$0.5B cash out not in the capex ratio.

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly driver set: revenue = four regional lines (ly x (1 + regional growth)), EBIT = revenue - cost of revenues - opex (both $M drivers), gross profit = revenue - cost of revenues. One leg carries the value: P/E 16.82x on the model's own NTM GAAP EPS at 2027-11-17 (no DCF for NFLX; no FCF leg since NFLX is not in the tech FCF-leg list). Driven share of revenue 100%.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) regional growth paths (2027 +8.5/9.5/10/12%): evidence-based alternatives are consensus FY2027 revenue $56.6B (+10.7%, MarketScreener [13], about +$2/share) and the base-rate fade path; (2) cost of revenues growth 7.5% vs the 2026 content-amortization guide of ~10% [4] (about -$3/share, under 5%); (3) exit P/E k = 0.8 default. No financing event above 20% probability (no deal pending after the WBD exit [5]; a $1B bond refinanced a maturity [1]). Drivers not yet approved by Kilian as a card (forecaster round). Research was limited by blocked pages (Zacks, MarketBeat, Northeast Times, chartmill).

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: NFLX trades at 16.33x NTM (59.68 / 3.655 [14]), 14% below the peer median; the exit 16.82x keeps most of that gap (k = 0.8).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No persistence case is argued beyond the default shrink: the discount reflects revenue growth slowing for four straight quarters (16.2% to 11.5% [1]) and losing TV-time share to YouTube [18][19], against peers with faster EPS growth (META +16%, GOOGL +16%, AMZN +33% [14]). DIS (16.6x) is the closest business and sits just below the exit multiple.
comps_summary.peer_count_flag: 6 peers: genuine listed comparables for a global subscription video platform are few. WBD and PSKY were left out (merger in progress, levered), ROKU (near-zero earnings), Chinese/Korean/Indian platforms (country distortion rule).
